title: Review: Monoclonal antibodies biology only ht only; Plant disease biology only; Photosynthesis
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for AQA GCSE Biology (8461) (status of the source: authored-gated-unreviewed). Terms and clues: 4.4.1.3-xt2 term and clue written for the game; 4.4.1-c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; 4.3.3.2-xt1 term and clue written for the game; 4.3.3-c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: 4.3.3-q02, 4.3.3-q04, 4.4.1-q01, 4.4.1-q04, 4.4.1-q07, 4.3.3-q01, 4.3.3-q03, 4.4.1-q02, 4.4.1-q03, 4.4.1-x01 (written for the game), 4.3.3-x01 (written for the game), 4.3.3-x02 (written for the game). Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Starch
items.clue: The insoluble substance into which plants convert glucose for storage

items.label: photosynthesis
items.clue: Carbon dioxide and water are converted to glucose and oxygen using light.

items.label: Waxy cuticle
items.clue: The tough, waterproof outer layer of a leaf that microorganisms cannot easily cross

items.label: Aphids
items.clue: Insects that infest plants and feed on them, taking dissolved sugars and other nutrients from the plant and so weakening it.

questions.stem: Which of these plant problems is caused by a fungal pathogen?

options.text: Black spot, giving dark marks on rose leaves
Aphid infestation, giving reduced plant growth
Chlorosis, giving yellow patches on leaves
Tobacco mosaic virus, giving a mosaic pattern

questions.explanation: Black spot is the named fungal disease of plants: purple or black spots develop on the leaves, which often turn yellow and drop early.

questions.stem: Which of these is a physical defence response that resists invasion of microorganisms?

options.text: Poisons which are made in the leaves
Hairs which grow on the leaf surfaces
Leaves which curl when they are touched
Layers of dead cells around the stems

questions.explanation: Layers of dead cells around stems (bark on trees), which fall off, are a physical defence response that resists invasion of microorganisms.

questions.stem: Which line shows the equation for photosynthesis written in chemical symbols?

options.text: CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and O2.
C6H12O6 and O2 react to form CO2 and H2O.
CO2 and O2 react to form C6H12O6 and H2O.
CO2 and H2O react to form C6H12O6 and heat.

questions.explanation: This is the equation carbon dioxide + water → (light) glucose + oxygen written with the chemical symbols CO2, H2O, C6H12O6 and O2.

questions.stem: A student plots the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed against light intensity at a constant temperature. The graph rises steeply and then becomes a horizontal line. Which statement explains the horizontal part of the graph?

options.text: Light intensity is still limiting the rate on the flat part.
The plant has switched from photosynthesis to respiration.
The rate is still rising but the graph is not showing it.
Another factor, such as temperature, is now limiting the rate.

questions.explanation: The factors interact and any one of them may be the factor that limits photosynthesis. Once light intensity is no longer limiting, temperature or carbon dioxide concentration limits the rate, so the rate stops rising.

questions.stem: How does a plant obtain the amino acids it uses for protein synthesis?

options.text: Amino acids are made from starch and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are made from glucose and nitrate ions.
Amino acids are absorbed from the soil by the roots.
Proteins are absorbed from the soil by the roots.

questions.explanation: Glucose produced in photosynthesis is used to produce amino acids, and to do this plants also use nitrate ions that are absorbed from the soil.

questions.stem: A plant has grown to the normal height for its age, but its leaves have turned yellow. What is the most likely cause?

options.text: A lack of nitrate ions, needed to make chlorophyll
A lack of magnesium ions, needed to make chlorophyll
An infection by black spot, a fungal plant disease
An attack by aphids, which are plant microorganisms

questions.explanation: Magnesium ions are needed to make chlorophyll, so a magnesium deficiency causes chlorosis, in which the leaves turn yellow while height can stay normal.

questions.stem: A rose plant has sharp thorns on its stems. Which type of plant defence is this?

options.text: A physical defence that resists microorganisms
A chemical defence that kills invading bacteria
A sign of infection by a fungal plant pathogen
A mechanical adaptation that deters animals

questions.explanation: Thorns and hairs deter animals, so they are listed as mechanical adaptations rather than as physical or chemical defence responses.

questions.stem: Which statement describes photosynthesis as an endothermic reaction?

options.text: Energy is transferred from the chloroplasts to the surroundings.
Energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts.
Energy is transferred from the surroundings to the mitochondria.
Energy is transferred from the glucose to the environment as heat.

questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is an endothermic reaction in which energy is transferred from the environment to the chloroplasts by light.

questions.stem: A student measures the rate of photosynthesis of pondweed by counting bubbles of oxygen. She counts 90 bubbles in 3 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis?

options.text: 30 bubbles per minute
90 bubbles per minute
270 bubbles per minute
0.03 bubbles per minute

questions.explanation: Rate is the amount of product divided by the time taken: 90 bubbles ÷ 3 minutes = 30 bubbles per minute.

questions.stem: A plant uses some of the glucose from photosynthesis to make cellulose. What is the cellulose used for?

options.text: Storing energy in an insoluble form
Making amino acids to build proteins
Strengthening the cell wall
Absorbing light for photosynthesis

questions.explanation: Cellulose is made from glucose and strengthens the plant cell wall.

questions.stem: A crop shows stunted growth, but its leaves are a normal green and no pests are found. Which deficiency is the most likely cause?

options.text: Magnesium ions, needed to make chlorophyll
Magnesium ions, needed to make proteins
Nitrate ions, needed to make proteins
Nitrate ions, needed to make chlorophyll

questions.explanation: Nitrate ions are needed for protein synthesis and so for growth; a lack causes stunted growth.

questions.stem: White dead-nettle leaves look like stinging nettle leaves, but they cannot sting. Animals avoid eating them. Which type of defence is this?

options.text: A chemical defence: poisons deter herbivores
A mechanical adaptation: mimicry tricks animals
A physical defence: a barrier stops microorganisms
A mechanical adaptation: stinging hairs deter animals

questions.explanation: Looking like a harmful plant is mimicry, a mechanical adaptation that tricks animals.
